newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN Amro picked to buy Hungary's MHB bank.
newsitem.headline: ABN Amro picked to buy Hungary's MHB bank.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN Amro has been chosen to buy Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB), Hungary's fifth largest bank, sources close to the transaction said on Thursday.
The official announcement was expected this week, possibly later on Thursday, after a meeting of the state privatisation agency APV Rt, the sources said.
"It means they now negotiate with them (APV) but their offer was deemed to be the best," one source said.
ABN Amro and Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein both had submitted bids in the one-round tender for the sale of an 89.23 percent stake in MHB.
The sources declined to say anything about ABN Amro's winning bid. APV officials have said previously that they hoped to complete the sale by the beginning of next year.
ABN Amro has a bank in Hungary but the acquisition of MHB would give it branch offices throughout the country.
In October, MHB said it posted an after-tax profit of 3.44 billion forints for the first eight months of 1996, compared with 1.4 billion after-tax profits for all of 1995.

Under the leadership of its chief executive officer Zsigmond Jarai, who took over at MHB in 1995, the bank has written off millions of dollars of bad debt, cut staff by 40 percent to 2,500 and reduced operating costs.
MHB has plans to regroup 40 of its branches in retail banking under a subsidiary called MHB Nepbank, and would have 30 branches specialising in corporate clients.
